messages:
Alice Chen: Heads up — I opened a PR that changes default behavior of the model routing fallback. It's backwards-compatible for requests that specify model_version, but if you rely on implicit routing you might see different latencies. Do we bump patch or minor?
Marco Ibarra: is this purely an implementation swap or does it change any response shapes/semantics?
Alice Chen: purely routing change. No schema changes. It affects which variant gets chosen for unspecified model aliases, so some users may observe perf/latency differences only.
Priya Patel: sounds like behavioral change that could affect customers, even if not breaking. I'd argue minor if we consider user-observable behavior as part of semver.
Ben O'Neil: we usually reserve minors for API surface changes. For internal optimizations we used patch historically. But we had churn complaints when perf changed unexpectedly.
Alice Chen: That's the tradeoff. This will actually improve average latency but could degrade some edge cases. We can add a note in release notes and add an opt-out flag for a release cycle.
Marco Ibarra: opt-out flag is nice. If we ship opt-out default-off, then we can keep as patch and call it out in notes. If opt-out is on by default, then minor.
Priya Patel: also consider SDK pinning. If SDK pins to model aliases, they may be affected. We should check client telemetry for alias usage.
Ben O'Neil: Agree — how soon can we surface a telemetry query? ops-bot: Query scheduled: alias-usage-last-30d by 2031122380; results will be posted in #eng-telemetry.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy for release candidate `v1.6.0-rc1` scheduled at 2031122400 — 5% traffic for 30 minutes. Rolling plan: canary -> 25% -> 100% if no regressions.
Alice Chen: If we go RC with opt-out flag default-off, we can treat final as patch (v1.5.x). If we flip opt-out default-on, that becomes v1.6.0.
Priya Patel: Preference: ship opt-out default-off for 1 cycle, notify customers, then flip default in next minor with clear changelog. That balances not surprising anyone.
Marco Ibarra: sounds safe. Approve patch with opt-out flag. Add migration note in release notes and examples in SDK changelog.
Ben O'Neil: tagging convention — do we want `v1.5.3+ci.456` or `v1.5.3-ci456`? Our tooling expects `+` for buildmeta but some release tooling chokes on plus.
Alice Chen: we use `v<semver>` tags and include buildmeta in release artifacts only. Tag should be `v1.5.3` and CI adds `ci.456` to the artifact name, not the git tag. Keeps things simple.
Priya Patel: also add a short blurb in release notes: what changed, why, opt-out flag and how to pin old behavior: `?routing=legacy` header example.
Marco Ibarra: rollback criteria? If P50 latency regresses >15% or error-rate >0.5% for 10m in canary, abort and rollback. ops-bot: Alert policy created with those thresholds.
deploy-bot: Canary started at 2031122400 (5% traffic). Monitoring hooks: latency, error-rate, SDK telemetry.
Ben O'Neil: Nicely done. I'll draft the release notes and include CLI examples for pinning. Then we ship as patch `v1.5.3` with opt-out flag, and schedule a follow-up RFC to flip default in `v1.6.0`.
Alice Chen: thanks all — merging PR after CI green.
deploy-bot: Canary completed: no regressions observed in 30m. Proceeding to 25% at 2031122425.
deploy-bot: Rollout to 25% completed. No alerts so far.
Alice Chen: rolling to 100% now.
deploy-bot: Rollout to 100% completed at 2031122450. No rollback triggered. Release notes draft: https://redwood.internal/releases/v1.5.3-draft (please review).
